ideas.description: On the current tip (E028 commit e95ff94: Muon NS3 batched and compiled, lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, 6.5 epochs), make one change: the Muon group's terminal lr floor goes from 0.07x to 0.15x. Shift the linear decay after warmup so it ends at 0.15x at the final step. Warmup shape, peak, the SGD group's schedule (floor stays 0.07x), lookahead, epochs and everything else stay unchanged. This is the untested direction opposite E025, where decay-to-0 cost 0.51 pp on the Muon group.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.0 to +0.35 pp, point +0.12 pp (range 0.749-0.760 around tip 0.7546). Time unchanged within ±1.5% (~6.08 s). A gain of 0.2 pp or more supports H1.6.4 and banks enough margin to retry 6.25 epochs (~-3.5% time); then try 0.25x. A drop of 0.15 pp or more means 0.07x is near the optimum, which closes the Muon-tail axis.

ideas.description: Systems change; the recipe is unchanged during the first epoch. On the tip, train the whitening-conv bias only for the first epoch (~49 of ~319 steps), as airbench94_muon/Hiverge do. After that, call a second compiled train-step variant where whiten.bias is detached / requires_grad=False. The whitening output then needs no grad, and the backward skips the input-gradient (dgrad) of block 1's first 24->128 conv at 31x31 plus the whitening-bias reduction. Compile and warm up BOTH variants in build() on synthetic data (full and partial batch) so the switch never recompiles in the timed region. Lookahead still blends the frozen bias (a no-op once it is fixed). Run drafts/debug_nan.py on both graphs under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs first.
ideas.expected: Time -1.5% to -3.5%, point -2.3% (~5.94 s). That conv's dgrad is ~54 GFLOP of ~1.8 TFLOP per step (~3%), skipped on ~85% of steps. Accuracy within ±0.25 pp of 0.7546 (re-draw plus a tiny effect from freezing a 24-element bias). If accuracy falls below 0.753 by re-draw alone, keep the code and pair it with the next accuracy gain. A time gain under 1.5% is inconclusive by H4.1.

ideas.description: On the tip, after training ends and the final lookahead-averaged weights are in place (inside train(), so it is timed), recompute the BN running statistics. Reset running_mean/var, set BN momentum=None (cumulative average), and run a no-grad train-mode forward over 12 batches of 1024 training images: un-augmented, normalized as in training, bf16 autocast, channels_last. Restore the momentum afterwards. Compile and warm up this train-mode no-grad forward in build() on synthetic data. Before launching, check in drafts/ whether lookahead currently blends BN buffers; recalibration replaces them either way. The learning recipe is otherwise unchanged.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.0 to +0.4 pp, point +0.15 pp (the averaged weights' activation statistics differ from the buffers accumulated along the fast trajectory). Time +0.8% to +2% (12 forwards at ~1/3 step cost ≈ 70-100 ms). A gain of 0.2 pp or more for 2% time or less supports H1.6.5 and allows 6.25 epochs at a net ~-2%. A gain under 0.1 pp refutes it: the buffers already match the averaged weights.

ideas.description: On the tip at 6.5 epochs, change only the label smoothing, from 0.2 to 0.1. E004 tested LS only between 0.2 and 0.3, and only on SGD at 9 epochs. Hiverge uses 0.09 at ~7.65 epochs. Everything else (Muon, SGD group, lookahead, augmentation, epochs) stays identical.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.3 to +0.4 pp, point +0.08 pp; time unchanged (±1.5%). A gain of 0.25 pp or more supports H1.7.2: short horizons want weaker regularization, which also raises the priority of H1.8.2 (drop translate). A drop of 0.2 pp or more closes the LS axis on the Muon base; then the 0.2-0.3 plateau seen on SGD holds here too.

ideas.description: Test whether reallocating FLOPs from block-1 depth to epochs pays now that the Muon epoch slope is steep (1.14 pp/epoch for 7.5% time between 6.5 and 7). On the tip, cut block 1 from 3 convs to 2 (drop one 128->128 3x3 conv) and raise epochs from 6.5 to 7.0, with all schedules scaled to the new step count. These are the two halves of one time-matched reallocation. The Muon NS group for 128x1152 now has one matrix instead of a pair; warm up the new shapes, including the 7-epoch final partial batch, in build(), and run the finite-gradient check.
ideas.expected: Time within ±1.5% of the tip (~6.0-6.15 s): E015 measured -7.5% from the conv cut, and +0.5 epoch adds ~7.7%. Accuracy -0.3 to +0.5 pp, point +0.17 pp (E015 measured -0.40 pp for the depth cut; +0.5 epoch is worth ~+0.57 pp). A gain of 0.2 pp or more supports H5.1.1/H5.1 and the depth-2 net becomes the base for further epoch trimming. Within ±0.2 pp supports H5's allocation indifference.

ideas.description: Systems change, math unchanged. Gate it first in drafts/: compare the batched Muon step's wall span (cuda events around it) with the sum of its kernel times from the profiler. Launch only if the gap is 0.4 ms/step or more. If so, capture the compiled Muon step (foreach Nesterov momentum, NS3 bmm per shape group, sqrt(out/in) scaling, weight-norm projection) in a torch.cuda.CUDAGraph during build() on synthetic tensors. Use static .grad buffers (zero_grad(set_to_none=False)), a 0-d lr tensor updated with fill_, and parameters and momentum buffers that prepare() resets IN PLACE (copy_/zero_), so the captured addresses stay valid across trials. Replay the graph each step. Everything else stays unchanged.
ideas.expected: Muon step from ~1.43 ms to 0.5-0.9 ms per step; mean time -1.5% to -4%, point -2.5% (~5.92 s). Accuracy identical to the tip up to re-draw (±0.2 pp). If the gate shows the 1.43 ms is mostly kernel time, not gaps, skip it and mark H2.4.4 refuted: the remaining Muon cost is FLOP- or bandwidth-bound.

ideas.description: On the tip, raise the batch size from 1024 to 1536 at 6.5 epochs (~212 steps instead of ~319), with all schedules scaled to the step count. The Muon lr stays at 0.16 (normalized updates). Scale the SGD group (BN biases, whitening bias, head) as batch size requires: if the code already uses airbench's per-example lr normalization (lr/bs), keep the configured values; otherwise scale the SGD lr x1.5 and keep lr*wd constant. Lookahead syncs every 5 steps as before. Warm up the new full and partial batch shapes in build().
ideas.expected: Time -3% to -6%, point -4.5% (~5.80 s): ~107 fewer Muon/lookahead steps (~0.15 s) plus larger GEMMs. Accuracy -0.7 to +0.2 pp, point -0.3 pp: one third fewer fixed-magnitude Muon rotations. That is likely infeasible at a 0.16 pp margin, but it tells us whether bs is a cheaper lever than epochs. If the drop is 0.15 pp or less, keep it, and the follow-up is Muon lr 0.20 at bs 1536. A drop above 0.5 pp refutes H1.2.3 and closes the batch-size axis.

ideas.description: On the tip, add per-image brightness and contrast jitter inside the compiled GPU augment, applied to the [0,1]-scaled images before normalization and whitening: x = (x - mean_img) * (1 + U(-1,1)*0.13) + mean_img + U(-1,1)*0.14, drawn independently per sample, with alternating flip and translate-2 kept. The RNG comes from the trial-seeded generator in prepare. Eval is unchanged. Warm up the new augment graph in build() on synthetic data.
ideas.expected: Accuracy -0.3 to +0.4 pp, point +0.1 pp; time +0.2% to +1% (one fused elementwise pass per epoch over 50k images). A gain of 0.2 pp or more for 1% time or less supports H1.8.1 and banks margin for 6.25 epochs. A drop of 0.2 pp or more means added difficulty hurts at 6.5 epochs, which raises the priority of H1.8.2 (removing translate).

structured_output.summary: The tip is E028: Muon at 6.5 epochs, 0.7546, 6.08 s. That leaves only a 0.16 pp margin over the 0.753 gate. The epoch slope is steep (~1.1 pp/epoch), so there are two ways to improve the score. The first is to bank accuracy and then cut to 6.25 epochs; the candidates are a higher Muon lr floor (H1.6.4, the untested opposite of E025), BN recalibration of the averaged weights (H1.6.5), LS 0.1 (H1.7.2) and brightness/contrast jitter (H1.8.1). The second is to save time at equal accuracy, using math-neutral systems cuts. The two cuts are freezing the whitening bias after epoch 1 to skip a ~3%-FLOP dgrad (H2.4.2) and a CUDA-graphed Muon step, gated on measured launch gaps (H2.4.4). Two explore runs probe allocation and batch size. One swaps a block-1 conv for +0.5 epoch at matched time (H5.1.1), which pays more now that epochs are expensive. The other is bs 1536 (H1.2.3). Every earlier queue item is done or dropped, so nothing needs dropping. H1.5.2 gets no idea because E029 already priced block-3 width at about half the epoch exchange rate.
